modules.name: :sdk:providers:tmdb
modules.owns: Implements the runtime's backend contracts using TMDB requests, internal DTOs and mapping. Owns TMDB authentication persistence and local reference profiles. The factory supplies runtime dependencies and returns StreamCoreClient.
modules.boundary: No application screen imports its DTOs or repositories. Optional artwork lives in the separate provider UI artifact.

modules.name: :sdk:runtime
modules.owns: Implements the public services. Coordinates account/profile state, capability checks, policies, local history/library/progress and lifecycle. Contains public integration contracts that providers implement, beside internal feature implementations.
modules.boundary: Does not depend on a concrete provider, a screen, Koin or a rendering engine. One RuntimeSession instance is shared by the client's services.

modules.name: :sdk:api
modules.owns: Defines StreamCoreClient and typed services. Also publishes pure validators and policies for immediate feedback. The runtime calls those rules too; callers cannot bypass enforcement by skipping form validation.
modules.boundary: No provider DTO, transport, DataStore or UI type in consumer signatures. Grouped search and playback keep related operations discoverable.

modules.name: :sdk:model
modules.owns: Immutable values, inputs, errors, results, capabilities and profile outcomes. Top-level names use the StreamCore prefix. Providers map their representations to these common types.
modules.boundary: No backend DTOs or visual layouts. Serializable saved content fields are also persistence contracts and deserve deliberate changes.

modules.name: :sdk:providers:clientB
modules.owns: Supplies the same integration contracts with a simulated backend and configurable reference profile scenarios. Useful for credential-free consumer journeys and substitution checks.
modules.boundary: Does not establish production backend coverage. Demo playback remains explicitly configured and identified.

modules.name: :sdk:testing
modules.owns: Holds shared ProviderContract journeys and result assertions in commonTest. Both providers include the directory in their test source sets and run the journeys from their own test functions.
modules.boundary: Registered with only Gradle's base plugin. No Kotlin or Android compilation, standalone test execution, production dependency or Maven publication.

modules.name: :sdk:ui
modules.owns: Resource-backed error presentation and avatar-resolution contracts plus shared strings. Consumers may opt into consistent wording and resources.
modules.boundary: No screens, navigation, Koin or application core:ui dependency. Headless SDK modules never depend on this artifact.

modules.name: :sdk:providers:tmdb:ui
modules.owns: TMDB avatar artwork, avatar ID mappings and provider-specific error wording.
modules.boundary: Separate from the headless TMDB provider; an external app can choose its own UI and resources.

modules.name: :sdk:providers:clientB:ui
modules.owns: ClientB avatar artwork and provider presentation adapters implementing the shared SDK UI contracts.
modules.boundary: Optional. Does not change the account, catalogue or progress behavior of the headless provider.

journeys.title: Create a client and restore its session
journeys.intro: Watch how a provider factory builds a shared runtime without making requests, then explicitly restores authentication. This follows Android TMDB assembly; platform creation differs on the browser.

steps.title: Create platform resources
steps.body: The host supplies Android context and typed configuration. The factory sets up the platform storage and HTTP client it owns. Construction does not authenticate or load the catalogue. Storage namespace ownership prevents conflicting live owners.
steps.effect: Allocates local resources; no network request yet.

steps.title: Supply backend implementations
steps.body: The factory creates TMDB API/error helpers and an authentication adapter, supplies a ProviderSessionFactory for future known accounts, and assembles the local stores. It passes these objects to RuntimeStreamCoreClient.
steps.effect: Concrete objects satisfy runtime-owned interfaces. No Koin is involved.

steps.title: Assemble one runtime
steps.body: One RuntimeSession is passed to the internal domain services. The same playback service handles progress and is also supplied to the library service for continue-watching observations.
steps.effect: The consumer receives StreamCoreClient and its typed public services.

steps.title: Restore authentication explicitly
steps.body: sdk.auth.restoreSession() returns StreamCoreResult<StreamCoreContext>. RuntimeAuthService implements it directly, serializes authentication work, checks the client is open, checks auth/context storage availability internally and asks AuthProvider.restoreSession() for StreamCoreResult<StreamCoreAuthState>. Once authentication is initialized, it returns the current context without repeating restoration, including after direct login. Login needs no prior restore call.
steps.effect: May check auth/context storage, read saved authentication and validate it with the backend.

steps.title: Install an account, not profile access
steps.body: A restored account must have a nonblank identity and satisfy any configured expected-account restriction. Runtime creates account-bound provider services, clears previous profile authorization and completes required selected-profile cleanup before publishing initialized account context.
steps.effect: The application must enter a profile before using profile-scoped content operations.

journeys.title: Log in with TMDB credentials
journeys.intro: There are two login contracts because the SDK's shared workflow and TMDB's protocol have different responsibilities.

steps.title: Enter the public service
steps.body: The application calls sdk.auth.login(identifier, password). It receives StreamCoreResult<Unit>. It reads the authenticated identity from sdk.context instead of treating a successful network response as all SDK setup being complete.
steps.effect: The app does not get a raw TMDB session or DTO.

steps.title: Validate and serialize
steps.body: The runtime checks credential-login capability, validates required inputs and trims the identifier. The password is not normalized. Authentication runs under the shared authentication mutex and checks auth/context storage availability before backend login.
steps.effect: Invalid input can stop the operation before backend calls.

steps.title: Run TMDB's protocol
steps.body: The provider requests a token, validates credentials against it, creates a session and discovers the actual account. It persists committed authentication and maps TMDB/network failures into SDK errors. This protocol belongs to TMDB, not to the shared runtime.
steps.effect: Backend requests and credential persistence occur here.

steps.title: Coordinate SDK context
steps.body: Runtime reads the provider's committed authState, validates account identity/restriction and creates account-bound services. It resets profile authorization and finishes required state installation. On cancellation it reconciles provider state and rethrows cancellation.
steps.effect: A provider can have committed authentication before a later operation fails. Observe sdk.context.

steps.title: Start profile entry
steps.body: The application asks profiles.beginEntry(). Depending on provider profiles, the result asks it to show no-profiles UI, choose a profile, request a PIN or continue with an already authorized profile.
steps.effect: Navigation is application-owned. Authorization is SDK-owned.

journeys.title: Load details for a profile
journeys.intro: This is a useful first content operation to read: validation, shared session checks, backend data and content policy in a short method.

steps.title: Validate content input
steps.body: The service rejects a blank content ID. It then invokes withAuthorizedProfile(profileId). Supplying a profile ID is not enough: it must correspond to the active authorization.
steps.effect: No content request runs for invalid input or invalid context.

steps.title: Check and refresh profile
steps.body: The guard checks authentication initialization, account and captured activation, then obtains current profiles from the provider. A missing profile revokes authorization; a changed profile replaces/revokes it and makes this call stale. Only a current matching profile reaches the block.
steps.effect: This provider profile fetch is real current behavior on every valid guard invocation.

steps.title: Fetch backend details
steps.body: The account's DetailsProvider implementation fetches and maps backend details into StreamCoreContent. TMDB DTOs stay inside its provider module.
steps.effect: Network and mapping occur in the provider; the service receives a common model.

steps.title: Apply content policy
steps.body: Before returning content, the runtime invokes ContentPolicyProvider. TMDB's reference policy interprets kids/adult metadata. It is not a universal numeric maturity-rating policy.
steps.effect: A direct details request cannot bypass applicable profile restrictions.

steps.title: Reconcile the result
steps.body: After suspending work, runtime checks that the account and profile activation still match. A SessionExpired error from the current account triggers credential invalidation and context cleanup. Obsolete results cannot invalidate a newer account.
steps.effect: A valid response for an old activation is returned as stale context, not current data.

journeys.title: Submit a catalogue search
journeys.intro: Typing, submitting, reusing displayed results and opening a result are different events. The app supplies intent; the SDK owns history rules.

steps.title: Capture and normalize
steps.body: search captures the active authorization and normalizes the query by trimming and collapsing whitespace. The search capability and profile context are validated. Fewer than three normalized characters produces an empty result after context checks.
steps.effect: UI debounce is separate and stays in the application.

steps.title: Query the provider
steps.body: For a searchable query, runtime calls SearchProvider.search with the normalized text, then applies the provider content policy to the returned items.
steps.effect: Results are common StreamCoreContent values restricted for the current profile.

steps.title: Decide whether to record history
steps.body: Typing does not record history. A successful nonempty Submitted or RecentSelected search records the query. The same captured authorization is carried into this operation.
steps.effect: A catalogue search can perform a second profile guard for its history operation.

steps.title: Persist one normalized entry
steps.body: The repository stores up to five recent queries per encoded account/profile key. Matching is case-insensitive; re-recording a query moves it to the front and preserves the newest spelling.
steps.effect: History is local SDK data, not a TMDB search endpoint feature.

steps.title: Return results with context checks
steps.body: A failed history checkpoint does not replace successful catalogue results. Cancellation still propagates and the original authorization must still be current. Explicit history operations report their own failures to the caller.
steps.effect: History persistence failure and catalogue failure deliberately have different user-facing consequences.

journeys.title: Add a title to My List
journeys.intro: This path has no backend library provider. Current library membership is SDK-owned local state.

steps.title: Capture context and timestamp
steps.body: The operation captures the active profile authorization and the clock value at entry. That timestamp describes the attempted membership change. No forwarding library adapter sits between this service and the store.
steps.effect: A later validation failure can happen after the clock was read, but before any store write.

steps.title: Check inputs and permission
steps.body: The service checks local-library capability, content ID and timestamp, then uses the shared profile guard. It checks the provider's policy on the content snapshot and confirms the activation again before writing.
steps.effect: Profile/content rejection prevents the membership write.

steps.title: Compute the owner key
steps.body: The storage key includes backend, storage namespace, authenticated account ID and profile ID, using length-framed components. Reusing a profile ID under a different parent account does not share the same saved bucket.
steps.effect: The store sees a partition key; the public API continues to speak profile IDs.

steps.title: Update membership atomically
steps.body: The repository updates its existing serialized library data. Liked and My List membership have independent timestamps; disabling one membership does not necessarily remove the other.
steps.effect: Storage serialization and transaction behavior live here.

steps.title: Observe logical collections
steps.body: The library observation combines policy-filtered membership entries with playback progress using the same captured authorization. It forms liked, My List and continue-watching collections. UI decides layout and focus.
steps.effect: New activation means creating a new observer. An old observer does not switch accounts automatically.

journeys.title: Report a playback checkpoint
journeys.intro: Source resolution, saved progress and player rendering are related but different. This follows progress reporting after the app has started its player.

steps.title: Create one recorder
steps.body: The service captures authorization and creates a private ProgressRecorder for this playback request. The recorder owns a mutex and lastAttemptedPeriodicBucket initialized from the starting position.
steps.effect: Two recorders share the service but have independent request/cadence state.

steps.title: Report an explicit event
steps.body: The application sends Periodic, Checkpoint or Completed plus position and duration. Completed removes saved progress even if duration is unknown. Other events with nonpositive duration skip without erasing saved progress.
steps.effect: The recorder does not run a timer, listen to Media3 or stop the player.

steps.title: Apply cadence
steps.body: A Periodic event attempts only when the integer position bucket (positionMillis / 10,000) exceeds the last attempted bucket. The bucket advances before storage, even on failure. Checkpoint bypasses this gate without resetting it.
steps.effect: Cadence is based on playback position, not elapsed wall-clock time.

steps.title: Enforce resume eligibility
steps.body: The validated update uses a pure rule: positive duration, position at least 30 seconds and fraction strictly below 95%. A resumable entry is upserted; otherwise the existing entry is removed.
steps.effect: Direct updateProgress applies this rule even for unknown duration. Recorder unknown-duration skipping happens earlier.

steps.title: Persist and return outcome
steps.body: The store persists progress under the captured account/profile partition, keeping the newest 50 entries per partition. Runtime returns a typed result, and cancellation propagates. The application's player-exit flow must finish despite an ordinary checkpoint failure.
steps.effect: Recording progress does not own navigation or player resource release.

journeys.title: Log out without erasing saved data
journeys.intro: Follow the normal success path, then compare transient failure and close. The distinctions protect both backend semantics and retained user data.

steps.title: Serialize authentication changes
steps.body: Logout runs under the authentication mutex, rejects a closed instance and checks auth/context storage availability before asking the provider to log out.
steps.effect: Login and logout use the same coordinator rather than racing independent service state.

steps.title: Ask the backend to revoke
steps.body: The provider handles TMDB session deletion and its committed credential state. A temporary remote failure must not silently become successful local logout. Cancellation can occur after backend/provider state has changed.
steps.effect: The backend adapter determines the protocol and classifies authoritative rejection.

steps.title: Clear SDK authorization on success
steps.body: For success or SessionExpired, runtime performs credential/selected-profile cleanup as appropriate and clears account/profile authorization in finally. Account-owned library, history and progress remain stored.
steps.effect: Signing into the same account later can recover its saved data.

steps.title: Keep lifecycle meanings distinct
steps.body: sdk.close() marks this SDK instance closed, cancels owned work and releases its owned resources once. It does not request remote logout or erase saved data. The host cancels its own context/flow collectors.
steps.effect: After close, create another SDK instance instead of trying to log in on the disposed one.
